Born in Saint Louis on 28 September 1883, son of Louis Jackson and Minnie Palmer.
Married Catherine Duffy of Brooklyn in 1910 and settled across the river in Hoboken,
at 911 Clinton Street. When he registered for the draft in September 1918 he was a watchman for the National Biscuit
Company at Tenth Avenue and 15th Street in Manhattan, the Nabisco bakery that is now Chelsea Market:
tall, with black hair and brown eyes. About 1932 the family moved to Bay Ridge,
Brooklyn, where he was the superintendent of an apartment building at 345 86th Street.
He died there of a stroke on 21 April 1934, aged 50.
Requiem mass at Saint Anselm's; buried at Saint John's Cemetery.
Born in Brooklyn in May 1892, the eldest child of Edward Henry Duffy, a peddler and later a driver,
and Frances Brady, both Brooklyn-born children of Irish parents, who had married in April 1891.
In 1900 the family lived at 31 North Elliott Place in Fort Greene, near the Navy Yard,
with her brothers Bernard and Edward and baby Frances, born there on 31 October 1899.
Her father very probably died suddenly of heart failure on 9 October 1903, at about 34;
by 1905 her mother had married Joseph Winchell, and she grew up as Catherine Winchell.
She married Francis P. Jackson of Saint Louis in December 1910, and they lived across the Hudson at Hoboken,
where Muriel was born. Widowed in 1934, she married William J. Wepprecht, who died in 1942,
and she died at West Hartford, Connecticut, in 1984.
